post.caption: The World's Chokepoints: Greenland. Erik the Red and the vanished Norse, Hans Egede and Danish rule, Truman's secret offer, Thule and the GIUK gap, self-government and the 2026 security deal. Images: public domain / CC0 (incl. NASA, USAF, US Space Force). Map data: Natural Earth.

erik.credit: Arngrímur Jónsson, Erik the Red, woodcut from Gronlandia (1688)

b36.credit: USAF, B-36 bomber at Thule Air Base (1950s)

pituffik.credit: US Space Force, Pituffik Space Base, Greenland

ice.credit: NASA / Michael Studinger, IceBridge flight over north-west Greenland (2013)

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does everyone want Greenland?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It's the largest island on Earth. About fifty-six thousand people live there, and most of it is buried under ice.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where is it, exactly?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Between North America and Europe. On the map it's American. Politically, it belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who got there first?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Arctic peoples, thousands of years ago. Then, around 985, the Norseman Erik the Red brought settlers from Iceland.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: According to the sagas, he called it Greenland so people would want to go there. The Norse farmed the south-west coast for four centuries.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Then they vanished. The last written record is a wedding at Hvalsey Church, in 1408. The Inuit stayed.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So how did Denmark get it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1721, the missionary Hans Egede sailed from Denmark-Norway. Colonial rule followed, and Greenland stayed Danish.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does America care?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Because of the map. Greenland, Iceland and Britain frame the GIUK gap, a sea gate between the Arctic and the Atlantic.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In the Cold War, Soviet submarines from Murmansk had to slip through it to reach the open ocean.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1946, President Truman secretly offered a hundred million dollars in gold for the island. Denmark said no. So the Americans built Thule Air Base instead.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Today it is Pituffik Space Base, watching for missiles over the North Pole.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Is Greenland still a colony?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Not any more. It got home rule in 1979 and self-government in 2009, with the right to choose independence.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So why all the headlines?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: As the ice melts, new sea routes and minerals open up. In 2025, Donald Trump said America needed Greenland, and would not rule out force.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In September 2026, the three governments signed a deal: more American bases, but Greenland stays in the Danish realm.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: the Taiwan Strait. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments what you think!
